title: Chapter 1 — Introduction to Datasets
objectives: Formalize datasets as empirical samples drawn from joint probability distributions under Data-Centric AI
Classify datasets across structural schemas (1NF relations, trees, manifolds) and temporal streaming dynamics
Analyze physical serialization layouts (row vs columnar stores, predicate pushdown, RLE/dictionary encoding)
Audit multi-dimensional quality frameworks, semantic defect typologies, and missingness mechanisms (MCAR/MNAR)
Execute four-tier exploratory data profiling across moments, Tukey IQR fences, and Simpson's paradox
Implement empirical risk minimization protocols, prevent data leakage, and optimize asymmetric economic thresholds
Govern dataset lifecycles through content-addressable versioning, RBAC masking, and cryptographic erasure

parts.title: Introduction to datasets
parts.bridge_in: This chapter establishes the core paradigm shift toward Data-Centric AI: defining an empirical sample mathematically, separating orthogonal records and attributes across computing paradigms, and analyzing the law of compounding data quality cascades.

parts.title: Types of datasets
parts.bridge_in: With records and attributes formalized, we classify datasets across two orthogonal axes: structural schemas (first normal form relations, semi-structured trees, and multimodal manifolds) and temporal dynamics (static historical snapshots versus dynamic streaming event queues with watermarks).
parts.split_reason: Section 1.2 is separated into structural/temporal types and physical serialization formats (sec:1.2.5) in part-03 to maintain focused learning modules.

parts.title: Dataset formats
parts.bridge_in: Format serializes structure onto physical media. We explore row versus columnar mechanical sympathy, formulate the mathematical I/O equations of analytical queries, and analyze advanced compression like dictionary and run-length encoding alongside Parquet predicate pushdown.
parts.split_reason: Continuation of sec:1.2 after types; keeps part under the 10-minute cap.

parts.title: Characteristics of good datasets
parts.bridge_in: Knowing on-disk structure is not enough—datasets must be fit for empirical modeling. We examine the five-dimensional quality framework, diagnose semantic accuracy catastrophes, classify missingness mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR), and engineer FAIR-compliant metadata sidecars.

parts.title: Exploring a dataset
parts.bridge_in: Exploratory data analysis is the forensic investigation that surfaces latent anomalies before training. We implement a four-tier inspection framework covering shape invariants, statistical moments (skewness and kurtosis), Tukey non-parametric outlier fences, and Simpson's paradox.

parts.title: Uses of datasets
parts.bridge_in: Datasets power empirical risk minimization and automated operational actions. We trace the closed-loop value cycle, analyze asymmetric error cost topologies, establish rigorous partitioning protocols to prevent data leakage, and optimize economic churn decision thresholds.

parts.title: Dataset management
parts.bridge_in: Long-term pipeline reliability rests on governance. We analyze the bronze-to-purge lifecycle, establish the six management pillars, implement immutable content-addressable versioning, enforce role-based dynamic column masking, and execute GDPR Article 17 cryptographic erasure.
